page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz, provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 512 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory density of 16 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Storage is bundled locally via a 3,780 GB NVMe SSD, providing high-capacity ephemeral disk resources without requiring standalone attached disks. The instance contains no discrete GPU accelerators and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core CPU throughput, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 10% alongside top-tier single-threaded compression and decompression performance. Multi-core performance is solid, evidenced by strong PassMark CPU scores and multi-threaded compression metrics, though stress-ng multi-core overall ranks within the middle tier due to the 32-vCPU configuration. Memory bandwidth benchmarks indicate steady mid-tier uncached throughput alongside strong overall memory subsystem responsiveness. Instruction set support is comprehensive, including AVX-512 vector extensions (with VNNI and BF16 support) and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. Text generation benchmarks for small language models show top-tier execution, though generation rates drop substantially on 70B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware.

The constrained vCPU configuration of the E64-32ads_v7 offers significant qualitative cost efficiency for software environments licensed per core, such as relational database engines, while still retaining the full 512 GB memory footprint and 3,780 GB local NVMe storage of the broader E64 chassis. The primary tradeoff lies in raw aggregate multi-threaded compute, which is halved compared to the unconstrained 64-vCPU variant. This server is best suited for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caches, data analytics pipelines, and memory-intensive ETL tasks requiring high local I/O and substantial RAM capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz. Configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 512 GB of RAM, it maintains an expansive 16 GB per vCPU ratio, which benefits workloads sensitive to per-core licensing fees. The instance integrates 3,780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI, while omitting discrete GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier single-core throughput and compression speeds, supplemented by strong PassMark scores and static web throughput. Its memory bandwidth and database operations demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution. With high memory density coupled with extensive local NVMe capacity, this instance is suited for enterprise databases, distributed in-memory caches, and memory-bound ETL workflows.
